mutations.note: SURVIVED on both engines: NaN<=x is false on both interpreter and strict VM, so the table walk recurses through all 60 remaining nodes and returns the last (3000 K end) node. The mutation is latent — it would only show up if a future test added a `ailang run --bytecode` gate. AC-W5 covers the spirit (VM/interpreter agreement) but not the specific failure mode.

mutations.mutation: M3: bbBpRp colour sign: +2.5*log10(BP/RP) instead of -2.5*log10(BP/RP)
M4: trapezoid end weight 0.5 → 1.0 in walk() (last element)
M6-weak: generator emits 16 sig figs in zBpRp (0.5906467146000018 → 0.590646714600001)
mutations.note: SURVIVED by tolerance: the 1.5e-15 absolute change is well below the 1e-9 check tolerance. Honest behaviour — the package is robust to this loss of precision.

mutations.mutation: M6-strong: generator truncates first colour node to 12 sig figs (-0.5698160690073688 → -0.569816069007)
M7: bbBpRpInvertible upper bound: firstOf(col) instead of lastOf(col)
M8: remove bpRp==bpRp guard from bbTeffFromBpRpExact (NaN treated as finite)
mutations.note: SURVIVED: bbBpRp(NaN) is NaN, so the bisection's bbBpRp(exp(m))>c comparison is false (NaN comparisons false on both engines), the recursion takes the 'else' arm every iteration, halves toward the LOW end, and after 48 steps returns ~3000 K. The bisection is self-defending. No test directly asserts bbTeffFromBpRpExact(nan)==3000.0 (test-coverage gap, not behaviour gap).

non_blocking.finding: M2's NaN guard in `lookup` is structurally fragile. Removing it has no observable effect today (both engines treat `NaN <= x` as false), but a future engine change could make it live. Recommend a comment in `lookup` noting 'this branch is the only reason NaN inputs deterministically return the 3000 K end node'.

bbTeffFromBpRpExact is not unit-tested for NaN. check07 covers exact-inversion accuracy at 4 finite points, but no test asserts bbTeffFromBpRpExact(nan()) == 3000.0. A 1-line addition would make M8 diagnostic instead of merely survive-by-accident.

V-from-G path is not exercised at interior colours. check11 calls it at bpRp=9.0 (clamped) and bpRp=NaN (clamped). A 0.5 < bpRp < 2.0 interior test would catch a silent sign-flip in bbGMinusVNodes(). The two-copies guard (check04) already ties the table to the forward model, so this is defence-in-depth advice, not a live bug.
